title: Rabbi Binyamin
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Akiva’s student, speaking in his name in [Semachot 9:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Tractate_Semachot.9.6): “Rabbi Binyamin says in the name of Rabbi Akiva: One rends the undershirt,” etc. He disagrees with Rabbi Elazar (ben Shamua, according to Hyman), as in [Ketubot 84a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.84a.17), where they said: “As the Tannaim dispute: Rabbi Binyamin says, ‘to the weakest of the claims, and that is proper’; Rabbi Elazar says,” etc.
He is likewise mentioned in baraitot in [Menachot 71a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.71a.10) and [Niddah 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.21b.14).[^1]

notes.text: Semachot’s afikarsin is a garment, here the undershirt. In Ketubot, Rabbi Binyamin means the claimant with the weakest proof. The passage names Rabbi Elazar without a patronymic. Hyman supplies ben Shamua.
